title: The Passions of Blood, Smoke, & Oil

content.text:
## The Passions of Blood, Smoke, & Oil

_aka, "The Passions of Blood, Smoke, & Fire"_

**DJ Jaya Prime**

\[[Stream on Mixcloud](https://www.mixcloud.com/JayaPrime/the-passion-of-blood-smoke-and-fire/)\]

27 songs and 20 quotes packed into just over 56 minutes. When I dropped the first production cut of this mix back in 2012, it was a full decade before the rest of the world would understand what it was actually about -- the cold beauty of the machine, the unpredictable fire of the human spirit, and the absolute absurdity and magnificence of the divine.

Initially, I was going to feature "Dreamstep" on the site instead, since it massively outperformed _The Passions_ over the years. I was just gonna shove this mix into the "[Others](other-dj-mixes)" tab and call it a day. But right as I was drafting this, a long-time fan shared _The Passions_ with her followers, adding: "Still my favorite 13 yrs later." So truly, thank you Nicky la Sanctionne ([Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/nicky_la_sanctionne)).

_This one goes out to you!_

## 2012, November 5 - Remember, remember...

The story of The Passions first spun out to a private audience on November 5th, 2012. The timing was incredibly heavy. We’d just found out the day prior that my brother Zero was after falling completely off the grid for a while. The house party I was mixing at wanted something with a lot more energy than "[Blood of the Moon](blood-of-the-moon)" -- or, in Flan's exact words: _"Ya know, but turn it up a notch!"_

  

This was still the Wild West era of SoundCloud, which was basically the bedrock for a cambrian explosion of underground creativity. Genres like future garage, UK 2-Step, and future bass that were once entirely confined to the name "Burial" had suddenly mutated into an entire community of artists forging new ground. I took that opportunity to pull my absolute favorites from the scene and weave them into a story.

  

I dropped a slightly updated version on SoundCloud just over a week later on the 17th. And while it never quite reached the viral heights of _Dreamstep_ or _Blood of the Moon_, the ones who loved it... _really, really_ loved it. That same family of _The Passions_ has kept it breathing over the years. That includes me, by the way -- I still listen to it religiously every single year on the 5th of November.

  

That very first time I DJ'd it live? That was also the last. Unlike my other mixes, I don't really get requests for this one. But in a weird way, that makes it special. It survives entirely on word of mouth... passed like a secret from one lover of the music to another.

## The Art of The Passions

I'm going into more detail with this one, because with exception to pages regarding her acting career, Helena nuked all her other online profiles. The album art came in thanks to **Helena Kenzo Rey**, another friend and collaborator from Burn as One dot Org and Deviant Art's "The Art of Smoking" group (see, "[Others](others)"). While I designed and colored the rest of it, nothing would be the same without her photo. Not only did she herself take the photo, as with many of her shots, but she's also the subject of the photo. Anyone who's tried to do the same will understand the difficulty level.

A few years before the pandemic, she got picked up for modeling, even appearing at The Met in NYC as a part of the incredible technology-driven Manus x Machina fashion line-up that mixed technology, fractals, and top-level craftsmanship to create moving luminescent clothing. Helena kicked off acting with a few non-speaking roles, then landed a supporting role in the cyberpunk thriller "Blackness". I was hoping at that point we'd see more of her. Instead, the pandemic hit, and what sites she hadn't nuked before were thrown into the void. I get it.

Despite her many additions to Burn as One, a fun fact is that she doesn't even smoke. She'd borrow her brother's smokes for the shot, then give 'em back. Wherever you are, Helena, you better be holding it down punk rock style. I'd expect nothing less.

## Extended Listening

The frenetic, fast-paced mixing style and quote-to-quote storytelling is easily rooted in "[The ADHD Revolution](adhd-revolution)", even though overall "The Passions" have a more cohesive theme for the story and selection of genres. The emotion though.. . the emotion is rooted in "[Blood of the Moon](blood-of-the-moon)" and that trip-hop, downtempo ambience. The audio graffiti on display here, however, would likely delight in adding visual elements from my [pop art fractal designs](other-pop-art).
